descript.abstract: This data release contains the compilation of country level mineral commodity production data extracted from Table 1 within all published 2019 international chapters in the U.S. Geological Survey's annual publication Minerals Yearbook Volume III: Area Reports — International. Individual Minerals Yearbook country chapters are published independently from the complete volume as "Advanced Release." Data reported in Table 1 of the individual country chapters include mineral commodity production data over a 5-year period (2015 through 2019). For this data release, these mineral commodity production data from all published 2019 international chapters were combined into a single table and reformatted into a machine-readable format .csv file. No content from the originally published tables were modified or revised in this process other than minor typographical errors.
descript.purpose: Published on an annual basis, the U.S. Geological Survey's Minerals Yearbook Volume III: Area Reports — International is the Government's publication to furnish information covering mineral commodities in various countries. Individual Minerals Yearbook country chapters include sections on government policies and programs, trade and production data, industry structure and ownership, commodity sector developments, infrastructure, and a summary outlook. Data tables within these chapters contain mineral commodity information and statistics over a range of 5 years covering over 90 individual minerals and materials. The purpose of this data release is to provide mineral commodity production data from these tables into a machine-readable format.

The burden for determining fitness for use of these data lies entirely with the user. Users are advised to read the dataset's metadata thoroughly to understand appropriate use and data limitations.

attracc.attraccr: All feature attribute values were peer reviewed for accuracy. Values were checked for correct data type and for presence / absence.

dataqual.logic: Data quality assurance and data quality control logic tests were performed for several feature classes. However, as many feature classes are directly from authoritative sources or from previously published governmental or scientific work, not all layers were subjected to a new logical accuracy test. Visual comparison of the feature classes supports the robustness of the overall data for feature classes not created by the National Minerals Information Center or from other programs within the U.S. Geological Survey.
dataqual.complete: Data set is considered complete for the information presented, as described in the abstract. Users are advised to read the rest of the metadata records, including data-level metadata records, carefully for additional details.

horizpa.horizpar: No formal positional accuracy tests were conducted.
